chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I have delayed in receiving sustenance.' So he (peace be upon him) got upset, then said to me, 'Say.'

O Allah, You have guaranteed my sustenance and the sustenance of every creature. O the best of those invoked, O the best of those who give, O the best of those who are asked, and O the most superior of those hoped from, do for me such and such.

key_terms.دَابَّة: Creature, beast (often used in Quranic context for all living beings)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication for delayed sustenance in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi*, this hadith highlights the spiritual remedy for anxiety regarding provision by shifting focus from the delay to Allah's inherent guarantee of sustenance for all creatures. The supplication employs a structure of divine attributes—specifically 'Khayr al-Mad'u' (the best of those invoked)—to emphasize the efficacy of calling upon God, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *tawakkul* (trust) coupled with active supplication. This narrative serves as a practical guide for believers to transform feelings of scarcity into confidence in divine generosity.
